correctness.rationale: Since A(K_n)=J−I, U_n(t)=exp(−it)[I+(exp(int)−1)J/n]. Its Schur transition probability is P^0+(n−2+exp(int)+exp(−int))P^1/n. For a Cartesian Kronecker sum, U(t) and M(t) tensor factor synchronously. Time averaging selects only zero Fourier frequencies. Tensor idempotents P_S then yield exact indexed eigenvalues and multiplicities; every coefficient is a sum of nonnegative weights (zero selection allowed exactly for n>=3), proving the signed-balance condition and the iff positive definite property. For three factors (2,m,n), all 4 sectors without the binary factor have positive λ and total rank mn; of sectors with binary factor only full sector can balance, iff |m−n|=2, restoring (m−1)(n−1) rank. Independent numerical spectral-projector Schur-square calculation gave ranks 12 for (2,3,4), 23 for (2,3,5), 39 for (2,4,6), 9 for (2,3,3), 4 for (2,2,2), and 9 for (3,3). One exact SymPy direct-rank attempt timed out; no impossibility inference was made, and analytic proof establishes the unbounded statement.
